sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Exception handling separates candidates who write happy-path code from candidates who write production-ready code. Every interviewer probes this because it's the clearest signal of professional coding habits at fresher level.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
The try/except/else/finally block has a specific contract:

```
try:       # the risky operation
except E:  # runs only if E is raised in try
else:      # runs only if NO exception was raised
finally:   # ALWAYS runs (cleanup goes here)
```

The `else` clause is the one 90% of candidates don't know. It's the distinguisher.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **Exception hierarchy** — `BaseException` → `Exception` → specific. Catch specific exceptions, never bare `except:`.
- **`raise` vs `raise e` vs `raise from e`** — `raise` re-raises current exception preserving traceback; `raise from e` chains for explicit cause.
- **`with` statement** — the idiomatic way to open files. Calls `__exit__` automatically even if an exception occurs.
- **Custom exceptions** — `class MyError(Exception): pass`. Add `__init__` only if you need a custom message or extra fields.
- **`FileNotFoundError`, `PermissionError`** — the two file I/O exceptions every interviewer expects you to name.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **'What does `finally` do?'** — always executes. Then follow-up: 'Can finally be skipped?' Yes: `os._exit()`, `SIGKILL`, power loss.
- **'What is the difference between `except Exception` and bare `except:`?'** — bare `except` also catches `SystemExit` and `KeyboardInterrupt`.
- **'How do you safely open a file in Python?'** — `with open(path) as f:` — the `with` ensures close even on error.
- **'What is the else clause in try/except?'** — the distinguisher question. It runs only when no exception occurs.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I always use a `with` statement for file I/O so the file is closed even if an exception occurs. I catch specific exceptions — FileNotFoundError for missing files, PermissionError for access issues — never a bare except because that swallows KeyboardInterrupt. The else clause is for code that should only run on success, keeping the try block minimal."*
